newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares slump amid dearth of buyers.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares slump amid dearth of buyers.

text.p: Danish share prices fell on Tuesday in a slack market, with dealers watching Wall Street for Wednesday's direction.

"We'll see what happens in the United States. It opened a bit lower but at about this time the index orders usually come. If they don't get the usual orders by closing time it will also be a day of falls (here) tomorrow," a Copenhagen dealer said.
The Danish KFX top-20 index closed 1.08 point down, at 166.02, in low overall bourse turnover of 627 million crowns.
"There were absolutely no buyers in the market," the dealer said.
Only four KFX shares bucked the downward trend.
GN Store Nord rose three crowns to 685.00, Chr. Hansen climbed 10 crowns to 770.00, Radiometer gained eight crowns to 368.00 and A.P.Moeller's D/S 1912 rose 5,000 crowns to 240,000.

Outside the top 20, prestige home electronics maker Bang & Olufsen rose 15 crowns to 380.00 after it agreed to buy back Dutch giant Phillips' 25 percent stake. --Carl Johan Corneliussen, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33 969657
